[2026-09-13T03:18:46+00:00] THE CROSSING TELEPORTED BACKWARDS BECAUSE THE HAND-OFF WAS FROZEN (games2, shipped c4dc6f3ef; maintainer 2026-09-13, direct). His five questions, answered from the code: (1) the destination zone does NOT boot — index.ts warmZoneRooms() warms every zone room at process start, autoDispose off, 16 warm rooms of the_game at ~20% of a core. (2) the data transfer is not the cost either — it is one bus set + get of a few hundred bytes. (3) the hand-off cannot be instant on a frame because it goes through the CLIENT: a new Colyseus room means matchmaking, a seat, a second WebSocket and a first state patch, which is hundreds of ms on a phone. (4) the old zone DID keep handling the body (its player loop never skipped a handing-off body) — but the hot state was written ONCE, at zone:go, so all of it was discarded. (5) so the new room adopted a body hundreds of ms old, and the client's own pending buffer had meanwhile been emptied by the OLD room's acks: reconciling onto the stale body lost exactly the distance covered during the join, then the input replay sprang it forward. That is the lag and the backwards teleport, and no faster join would have removed it. FIX: refreshHandoff rewrites the hot document every tick under the same capability (live x/y/elev/hp and the acked seq; a knockback, fall, current or hit is carried, not only what the client can replay), and the client replays from the seq the NEW room reports while rebuilding `pending` from predLog, the same input records kept past their ack. MEASURED (server/test/handofffresh.test.ts): the body runs 76 wu during the join and is adopted 0.0 wu from where the old room has it, seq 0 -> 13; with refreshHandoff disabled the same test adopts it 76 wu behind. Full suite: the same 12 pre-existing failures; typecheck clean. STILL OPEN, his own requirement: monsters. A remote body takes the server position raw (no interpolation anywhere in WorldScene), so a body seen as a GHOST across a border updates at EDGE_TICKS=2 = 10 Hz against 20 Hz in its own room — half the rate, twice the step. Next unit.
